# Painting the hallway

Easter weekend 2025. Hallway, stairs and landing. Been putting it off since we moved in. Writing down every product and quantity because next time I will not remember.

## Before

- Woodchip on the stairwell wall (why) and magnolia everywhere else
- Scuffs at bike-handlebar height all down one side
- Cracked filler line where I'd cut in the new switch drop in 2023
- Dado rail with about six layers of gloss on it, drips included
- Stairwell is about 4.6m to the ceiling at its highest point, so needed a proper setup

## Access

Borrowed Dean's (work) Werner combination ladder plus a 2.4m staging board. Combination ladder in the A-frame on the half landing, board across to the third stair. Felt fine once it was set and I'd checked it twice. Didn't overreach, moved the board instead. My back still knew about it on Tuesday, see [[Lower back pain]].

## Prep (the actual work)

### Woodchip off

- Steam stripper hired from HSS Hire Bristol, £32 for the weekend, booking ref HSS-B-660281
- Took most of Good Friday. Woodchip came off in sheets once it got going
- Plaster underneath was rough in places and blown behind the old thermostat spot

### Filling and sanding

- Patched the blown bits with Thistle Multi-Finish, 25kg bag, used about a quarter
- Small dents: Toupret, same as in [[Drywall patching]]
- Sanded everything with 120 grit on the pole sander, dust sheets everywhere, hoovered twice
- Sugar soap wash on the woodwork, then 180 grit key on the gloss

### Stain block

There was a water stain on the landing ceiling from an old leak (pre us). Two coats of Zinsser BIN shellac primer or it would bleed through emulsion forever.

## Colours

Spent way too long on this. Tester pots on A4 card, taped up for a week, looked at them morning and evening.

- Walls: Little Greene "French Grey Mid" (No. 162), Intelligent Matt Emulsion
- Ceiling: Dulux Trade Diamond Matt, Pure Brilliant White
- Woodwork (skirting, dado, spindles, doors): Little Greene Intelligent Eggshell, "Slaked Lime Deep"
- Front door inside: left as is for now

Lucía voted for a dark green below the dado. Vetoed for now. Might happen.

## Quantities and cost

| Item | Qty | Price |
|---|---|---|
| French Grey Mid 5L | 2 | £148 |
| Ceiling white 5L | 1 | £39 |
| Eggshell 2.5L | 1 | £71 |
| Zinsser BIN 1L | 1 | £22 |
| Frog tape, rollers, sleeves | | £34 |
| Steamer hire | | £32 |

Total about £346. Walls took a mist coat plus two full coats. Used nearly all of the second 5L tin.

## Order of work

1. Ceiling first, all of it
2. Walls, top down, cut in with a 2" Purdy and rolled with a 9" medium pile
3. Woodwork last, two coats eggshell, 16h between
4. Took the hallway radiator off the wall to paint behind it. Drained just that rad: closed both valves, counted the turns on the lockshield (3.5), undid the unions into a tray. Painting behind it was worth it. Refilled and bled after, same method as [[Bleeding radiators]]

## What I'd do differently

- Start the woodchip on Thursday night, not Friday morning
- Buy the eggshell in the bigger tin, ran short on the spindles
- Don't paint spindles. Ever. Spray or pay someone

Written up properly a few weeks later, see [[2025-03-14]] for when we first argued about the colour.
